newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Burundi reopens border with Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Burundi reopens border with Zaire.

text.p: The border between Burundi and the Democratic Republic of the Congo reopened on Tuesday a year after regional states imposed sanctions on Burundi following an army coup, witnesses said.

"This is a normalisation between our countries. The border on the Burundian side was always open. This morning the Congolese side was opened," Burundi's interior minister Lieutenant-Colonel Epitace Bayaganakandi told Reuters.
Bayaganakandi and Congo interior minister Mwenze Kongolo drove from the Burundian capital across the border to Uvira in the former Zaire during the opening ceremony.
Regional states imposed sanctions on Burundi last July and closed their borders after the Tutsi-dominated army brought Pierre Buyoya to power and ousted a Hutu president.
Burundi offered political and moral support to Laurent Kabila's rebellion which in May culminated in him taking power.
Sanctions, relaxed in April, have failed to stop a steady flow of goods reaching Burundi on the blackmarket, according to Bujumbura residents.
